summary: Ann Gleig is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Jeffrey J. Kripal (attested 2010).

Ann Grodzins Gold is an indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD in anthropology at the University of Chicago (~1970–1984) and held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993–2021).

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She held posts at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University, where she served as director and permanent member (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler is a historian who studied at Barnard College (~1968–1972) and Columbia University (~1972–1976). She taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989) and University of Michigan (1989–2004) before becoming founding director at The New School (2004).
Anna Andreeva is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Heidelberg University and holds a permanent membership at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an indologist who studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Würzburg, and the University of Tübingen (MA, 1998). She held posts at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS under Lionel Caplan (by 2002) and held positions at the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 2002) and Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (2002).

Anna Brown is a scholar of religious studies who studied Zen under Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). She served as chair of the political science department and director of the social justice program at Saint Peter's University (attested 2017).

Anna Filigenzi is a specialist in archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She held posts at the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (director, 2003), University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012), and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Munich and Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein, she worked at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1969) and the Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She held posts at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (~1976–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and New York University (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned her PhD at Uppsala University (completed 2007) under the supervision of Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada.
Annarao Kulkarni is a scholar in Indology and computational studies who held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anne Carolyn Klein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia (~1974–1981) under Jeffrey Hopkins and later served as Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University (~1991).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard University and held teaching posts at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and Harvard University (from 2002).

Anne Feldhaus is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, ~1971–1976), and was a Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University (from 1981).

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1993–1999). She held a post at the University of Texas at San Antonio (2000).

Anne Hopkins Aitken was a figure in religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Scripps College (~1928–1932), Stanford University (~1935–1937), Northwestern University, and the University of Oxford, and co-founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha (1959) and Maui Zendo.
